Simulate the spatio-temporal biomass operating truth

Source: R/biomass_simulate.R
simulate_biomass.Rd

Generates a completely known biomass trajectory for every year and cell of the spatial domain: total biomass from a surplus-production model, distributed in space by a static habitat (latitudinal envelope, hotspots, gradient, persistent random field), a redistribution of the envelope in time (e.g. poleward expansion) and spatio-temporal noise. No fishing process is simulated here (see simulate_fishery()).

Usage

simulate_biomass(
  cfg = om_biomass_config(),
  domain = NULL,
  long_table = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

cfg

Biomass configuration (om_biomass_config()).

domain

Optional spatial domain (om_domain_iccat(), om_domain_grid(), om_domain_from_gpkg()). By default it is built from cfg$spatial. Its regions take precedence over the ones in cfg$spatial.

long_table

If TRUE, also builds the long table Year x Cell ($table), the main product of Experimento 02.

verbose

Print progress messages.

Value

An object of class om_biomass, a list with cfg, dom (domain), pop (B_total and related series; attribute "ref" with reference points), base (static components), envelope, noise, logD, weights (p), biomass (B, cells x years, t), envelope_params and table.

Details

With om_biomass_config("BET_ICCAT") the result is identical, bit for bit, to Simulacao_Biomassa/outputs/data/biomass_true_base.rds of Experimento 02.

The caller's random number stream is left untouched: the simulation seeds its own stream with cfg$general$seed and restores the previous state on exit.

See also

check_simulation(), regional_summary(), make_biomass_figures(), om_write_biomass().

Examples

# \donttest{
sim <- simulate_biomass(om_biomass_config(), verbose = FALSE)
sim
#> <pelagicOM biomass truth> label 'base' | seed 20261005
#>   10051 cells x 76 years (1950-2025) | stock area BET-A
#>   B_total: 950,000 t (1950) -> 318,101 t (2025) | B/K 0.95 -> 0.32 | Bmsy 5e+05 t
#>   regional share: R01 0.04 -> 0.14 | R02 0.93 -> 0.74 | R03 0.03 -> 0.13 
head(sim$pop)
